historical_reviews.deepseek: The exact-name read can only corroborate backend telemetry; it does not prove the Web rendering or module mapping, and the inlet-sensor oracle is unrelated.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires protected UI/reviewer evidence and BF3 port/transceiver mapping.
historical_reviews.history: Duplicate row 1882 covers two GB inlet sensors and completed related reviews describe their airflow-location semantics; none supplies BF3 module evidence.
historical_reviews.v3_1: BF3 transceiver/module temperature must be tied to the populated port and module identity, not confused with the prior BF3 controller junction or later chassis inlet sensors.

original_test_intent: Verify that the BMC Web TEMP_BF3_Trans entry represents the intended BF3 transceiver and that its rendered value, units, status, thresholds, freshness and range match the approved module SPEC.
original_method: Verify target, BF3 port and populated transceiver; capture the protected Web row and page context; bind the resource to its physical module; compare complete fields to the approved transceiver SPEC; optionally correlate the same backend telemetry; preserve logs and make no port, module or thermal changes.
manual_activity: A platform reviewer validates the BF3 port/module identity and confirms the complete Web row against the correct transceiver thermal SPEC.
required_inputs: Units, thresholds, range and freshness rules
safety_requirements: Do not alter BF3 ports, modules, thresholds, cooling, power or firmware
Reject BF3 chip and GB inlet substitutions
Reject stale, missing, duplicate or unmapped data
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, route and BF3 port/module
Compare reading, units, health, thresholds, timestamp and module range
engineer_actions: Approve port/module mapping and transceiver SPEC
Resolve missing, stale or ambiguous module identity

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The exact backend name is a possible cross-check, but the truncated fallback and GB-inlet oracle do not cover the Web resource or BF3 module identity.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture the authoritative Web row first; use an untruncated exact-resource backend read only after proving it maps to the same port/module.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Web/SPEC check and 3/3-minute estimate remain; generic clearing and inlet-sensor substitution are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the Web resource to the actual populated BF3 port/module and retain its complete fields, freshness and module-specific limit result in one evidence object.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds physical module identity and staleness controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A controller-chip or chassis-inlet temperature can look reasonable while saying nothing about module thermals.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: If no transceiver is populated, expected absence must come from the approved topology rather than being judged as failure automatically.

project_override_considerations: Define the BF3 port, module population and module limit. The prior BF3 chip and duplicate GB-inlet cases stay separate; backend-only evidence needs approved UI equivalence.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/Web route, BF3 port/module identity and module SPEC
Protected UI capture with filter/refresh context
Mapping, reading, units, health, thresholds, timestamp and range result

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Web procedure and SPEC criterion coherently target the BF3 transceiver. Generic clearing and the inlet expected-output text are method/reference defects.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Port/module mapping, SPEC and protected UI are normal package inputs; execution becomes BLOCKED if the transceiver identity cannot be resolved after obtaining them.

review_improvement: Separates BF3 module thermals from controller-junction and chassis-inlet telemetry while preserving the intended Web/SPEC comparison.
independent_technical_reasoning: A transceiver contains its own thermal source and vendor envelope, and it may be absent or replaced independently of the BF3 controller. Therefore acceptance must prove module population and port association before applying a limit; neither a neighboring chip sensor nor an inlet reading can establish module health.
